comment: The HUMAN-OWNED cells of docs/HONESTY-MATRIX.md — the 'reachable via shipped policy DX?' column ONLY. Every other column is derived by lake exe honesty_matrix + scripts/honesty-matrix.mjs, and the renderer rejects an entry that tries to assert a derivable column. Each entry must carry who asserted it and when; the renderer refuses to render without both. Re-assert (update the date) whenever the shipped DX changes. NOTE 2026-07-16: the 2026-07-15 assertions said the shipped DX was hand-authored JSON and that 'workstream A never happened'. That was WRONG WHEN WRITTEN, not stale: seal-assurance-kit already shipped `seal init`, four recipes, and `seal add-kernel`. The DX did not change; the human read one repo and asserted about the product. Every cell below was re-established by RUNNING the CLI, not by reading its docs.

entries.value: yes — scaffolded by `seal init`; present in every recipe
entries.rationale: Executed 2026-07-16: `seal init <manifest>` (seal-assurance-kit) emits a policy whose only kernel section is `safety`, deriving one rule per tool from the manifest. All four recipes include S. `seal add-kernel S` REFUSES ('already present; refusing to overwrite existing policy edits'), which is fail-closed. The scaffold is a starting point and says so: it labels rules `_seal_scaffold` and warns 'annotations are trusted input, not verification' for every readOnly the server self-describes. Reaching a RUNNING gate still requires signing the policy and passing --pubkey to the host; the CLI does not sign.

entries.value: yes — `seal add-kernel T`; emitted by the prod-db recipe
entries.rationale: Executed 2026-07-16: `seal add-kernel T` prints 'added kernel temporal (T) — ACTIVE' and the policy gains a `temporal` section; `seal init --recipe prod-db` emits safety+temporal+budget. Note the column is about AUTHORING: the kernel itself is wired unconditionally (see the derived 'wired' cell), so an absent section means no temporal constraints, not an absent kernel.

entries.value: yes — `seal add-kernel C`; emitted by the deploy recipe
entries.rationale: Executed 2026-07-16: `seal add-kernel C` prints 'added kernel consensus (C) — ACTIVE' and the policy gains a `consensus` section; `seal init --recipe deploy` emits safety+consensus+linear. CONFIG.md documents the hand-authored shape (roster, votes_file, high_stakes) for anyone not using the CLI.

entries.value: yes — `seal add-kernel V`; emitted by the mesh recipe
entries.rationale: Executed 2026-07-16: `seal add-kernel V` prints 'added kernel convergence (V) — ACTIVE' and the policy gains a `convergence` section; `seal init --recipe mesh` emits safety+convergence. CONFIG.md documents the hand-authored shape (replicated tools).

entries.value: experimental only — `seal add-kernel K --experimental`; no recipe emits it
entries.rationale: Executed 2026-07-16: `seal add-kernel K` REFUSES without the flag ('EXPERIMENTAL K REFUSED: rerun with --experimental only after reviewing its non-claims') and warns 'CALIBRATION (K) IS EXPERIMENTAL and is outside every recommended recipe'; with --experimental it adds the section. No recipe emits K. So K is reachable but deliberately harder to reach than the other six, and that asymmetry is the honest content of this cell. CONFIG.md also documents the double gate: a present section with enabled:false is explicitly inactive (PRESENT-BUT-INACTIVE).

entries.value: yes — `seal add-kernel L`; emitted by the deploy recipe
entries.rationale: Executed 2026-07-16: `seal add-kernel L` prints 'added kernel linear (L) — ACTIVE' and the policy gains a `linear` section; `seal init --recipe deploy` emits safety+consensus+linear. CONFIG.md documents the hand-authored shape (grants_file, tools).

entries.value: yes — `seal add-kernel B`; emitted by the prod-db and token-governor recipes
entries.rationale: Executed 2026-07-16: `seal add-kernel B` prints 'added kernel budget (B) — ACTIVE' and the policy gains a `budget` section; `seal init --recipe prod-db` emits safety+temporal+budget and `--recipe token-governor` emits safety+budget. Strongest evidence in this column: the Golden Path filesystem leg drives `seal init` then `seal add-kernel B` to ACTIVE {S,B} end-to-end on a CLEAN CI runner, so this cell is corroborated by automation rather than by a human running it once.

Re-established 2026-07-16 against the CLI as well as the docs: nothing in CONFIG.md or the config parser (Host/Config.lean) names this kernel, the kit's validator knows only the seven sections (src/trusted-config.cjs), and `seal add-kernel` accepts only S/T/C/V/K/L/B — there is no letter and no JSON key a user could write that selects it. Consistent with the proof (Ffi.byteConsensus_never_registered) but asserted separately: absence from the DX surface is a human reading, not a theorem.
